facts.fact_text: The first applicant, Yılmaz Yıldız, is the branch chairman of the Health and Social Services Workers' Union (Sağlık ve Sosyal Hizmet Emekçileri Sendikası – 'the SES') in Niğde.
The second applicant, Kamiran Yıldırım, is the branch chairman of the Health and Social Services Workers' Union (SES) in Mardin.
The third applicant, Mehmet Metin Çılgın, is a member of the Health and Social Services Workers' Union (SES) in Mardin.
On 4 February 2005, several members of the Health and Social Services Workers' Union (SES) gathered in front of the Niğde Social Security Institution (Sosyal Sigortalar Kurumu – 'the SSK') Hospital.

The first applicant, Yılmaz Yıldız, read out the Health and Social Services Workers' Union (SES)'s press statement drawing attention to the problems that could arise as a consequence of the transfer of hospitals incorporated in the Social Security Institution (SSK) to the Ministry of Health.
The Health and Social Services Workers' Union (SES) press statement was addressed to the press and the public.

On 25 February 2005, the second applicant, Kamiran Yıldırım, and the third applicant, Mehmet Metin Çılgın, together with another thirty persons gathered in the Mardin Yenişehir Social Security Institution (SSK) Hospital yard.
The second applicant, Kamiran Yıldırım, read out the press statement in his capacity as chairman of the Mardin branch of the Health and Social Services Workers' Union (SES).
The police did not interfere with the demonstration on 4 February 2005 in Niğde or the reading out of the press statement.
The police did not interfere with the demonstration on 25 February 2005 in Mardin or the reading out of the press statement.

According to the police report of 4 February 2005 in Niğde, the group of demonstrators had been warned verbally that their gathering was illegal and ordered to disband for the protection of public order and safety.

According to the police report of 25 February 2005 in Mardin, the group of demonstrators had been warned verbally that their gathering was illegal and ordered to disband for the protection of public order and safety.

The Niğde public prosecutor filed an indictment charging the applicants with intentionally disobeying orders issued by the authorities aimed at protecting public order and safety, pursuant to section 32 of the Misdemeanours Act, Law No. 5326.

The Mardin public prosecutor filed an indictment charging the applicants with intentionally disobeying orders issued by the authorities aimed at protecting public order and safety, pursuant to section 32 of the Misdemeanours Act, Law No. 5326.
On 8 June 2005, the Mardin Magistrates' Court convicted the applicants as charged and imposed on them administrative fines of 100 Turkish liras (TRY) (approximately 62 euros (EUR)).
On 14 July 2005, the Niğde Magistrates' Court convicted the applicants as charged and imposed on them administrative fines of 100 Turkish liras (TRY) (approximately 62 euros (EUR)).
On 20 June 2005, the Mardin Assize Court dismissed the applicants' appeals against the Mardin Magistrates' Court decision.
On 26 July 2005, the Niğde Assize Court dismissed the applicants' appeals against the Niğde Magistrates' Court decision.
On 23 August 2005, the applicants paid the fines to the relevant tax departments.
On 11 October 2005, the applicants paid the fines to the relevant tax departments.

Section 32 of the Misdemeanours Act (Law No. 5326) provides that persons acting contrary to orders given by the competent authorities for the protection of public safety, public order and public health shall receive an administrative fine of 100 Turkish liras.

Section 9/ç of the Provincial Administration Act (Law No. 5442) provides that governors may issue and announce general orders to exercise the authority conferred on them by, and perform duties in connection with, laws, by-laws, regulations and government decrees.

Section 11/C of the Provincial Administration Act (Law No. 5442) provides that governors shall have the duty, inter alia, to secure peace and security, physical integrity, safety of private property and public well-being, and the authority to exercise preventive law enforcement.
According to Ministry of the Interior Circular no. 2004/100, authorised governors, having assessed safety needs, may prohibit the making of press statements close to critical institutions.

Under section 66 of the Provincial Administration Act (Law No. 5442), the local civil administration and local governors may impose penalties under section 32 of the Misdemeanours Act (Law No. 5326) on those who do not comply with decisions and measures taken in accordance with the applicable rules.
Section 6 of the Meetings and Demonstrations Act (Law No. 2911) empowers the most senior local governors to make and announce necessary regulations regarding demonstrations.
The Press Bulletin of the Governorship of Mardin dated 20 July 2004 declared unlawful the making of press statements within 100 metres of hospitals.
The Press Bulletin of the Niğde Governorship dated 5 August 2004 declared a prohibition on public statements made in front of any State institution or organisations and their outbuildings.
